sourceType: Independent original practice questions based on publicly listed exam or MCQ topics; not verbatim UNISA paper questions
sourceLimitations: These are newly written MCQs based on themes in the linked public source, not exact original paper wording. Some source previews are incomplete. Use the Source link to view the original where available.

questions.text: Which activity is least likely to be recorded by a transaction processing system?
options: An informal internal email between colleagues
questions.correctAnswer: An informal internal email between colleagues
questions.explanation:
TPS is used for routine business transactions. An email conversation is communication, not necessarily a recorded business transaction.

Student note: Do not treat every computer activity as a TPS transaction.

questions.text: In the value chain, developing technology that supports production is normally what type of activity?
questions.explanation:
Technology development helps several parts of the business operate and is one of the value chain's support activities.

Student note: Operations are primary; technology development is support.

questions.text: A company assembles and packages products for sale. In the value chain, this is normally ...
options: Human resource management, a support activity
questions.explanation:
Operations convert inputs into finished products or services; they directly create value.

Student note: Primary activities also include logistics, marketing/sales and service.

questions.text: Customers can move to a competitor without paying an exit fee. What tends to happen to customer bargaining power?
options: It becomes impossible to compare prices
questions.explanation:
Low switching costs make it easier for customers to leave, giving them more choice and bargaining power.

Student note: High switching cost can reduce customer bargaining power.

questions.text: What enables a virtual company to coordinate resources belonging to different partners?
questions.explanation:
Digital communication and networks allow virtual businesses to coordinate partners and resources.

Student note: Network collaboration can be global.

questions.correctAnswer: An explanation of how a business creates and earns value
questions.explanation:
A business model describes customers, offerings, costs, revenue and how the organisation operates.

Student note: A new business model can create competitive advantage.

SaaS means users access vendor-hosted applications as a service, often with a subscription.

Student note: SaaS is an application delivery model, not a hardware type.

questions.text: Which technology is used to exchange standard business documents such as purchase orders between organisations?
questions.explanation:
EDI allows systems at different organisations to exchange structured business documents using agreed formats.

Student note: EDI helps automate repeated business-to-business transactions.

questions.text: A manager starts with total sales and then opens sales by branch and by product. What BI action is this?
questions.explanation:
Drill-down lets a user move from a high-level summary to more detailed views.

Student note: Drill-down = go deeper; roll-up = summarise upwards.

questions.text: An online store sells directly to buyers instead of using several retailers. What is this called?
questions.explanation:
Disintermediation removes intermediaries in a distribution channel and may reduce costs.

Student note: The customer may pay less because fewer middlemen are involved.

questions.text: Which tool best presents key performance indicators on one screen?
questions.explanation:
Dashboards combine important measures in charts and indicators so managers can monitor performance.

Student note: A dashboard shows a quick overview; drill-down reveals details.

questions.text: Which system is designed to support a company's communication with customers during sales and service?
questions.explanation:
CRM helps teams follow customer interactions, service cases and sales activity in one place.

Student note: CRM deals with customers; ERP integrates internal processes; SCM coordinates supply.
